findings.title: State-mutating action performed via GET request
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe is only reachable via GET routes (config/routes.rb: `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) yet it mutates `TopicUser#notification_level` and persists it with `tu.save!`. GET requests are expected to be idempotent/safe; browsers/email clients routinely prefetch or re-request GET URLs (link previews, safe-link scanners, page refresh), and because the user must already be logged in (added to `ensure_logged_in`), a logged-in user who simply reloads the unsubscribe page, or who is tricked into navigating to this URL from a third-party page (GET requests are not blocked by SameSite=Lax on top-level navigation), will have their notification level silently changed again. Worse, the toggle logic is not actually idempotent: on the second invocation it moves the state from `regular` to `muted`, progressively down-grading notifications on every reload instead of leaving state unchanged. This should require POST/PUT with explicit CSRF protection, or be made properly idempotent.

findings.title: Possible NoMethodError when TopicUser record does not exist
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (e.g. if the TopicUser row for this user/topic was never created or was deleted), and the following code immediately calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.notification_level =`, which will raise NoMethodError on nil and return a 500 error instead of gracefully handling the case. There is no `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by` fallback or nil guard.

findings.title: Template placed at wrong path for the new top-level 'topicUnsubscribe' route
findings.body: The route is registered as a top-level, non-nested route: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' });` in app-route-map.js.es6, and its matching controller/view files are dasherized at the top level (`controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`, `views/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6`). However the template is placed in a nested folder as `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which is the convention used for routes nested under the `topic` resource (e.g. topic.fromParams), not for a standalone dasherized route name. This mismatch is likely to cause the Ember resolver to fail to find the template for the `topicUnsubscribe` route, breaking the newly added feature entirely.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link translation now requires unsubscribe_url, breaking other callers of build_email
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` i18n string (config/locales/server.en.yml) now contains a new interpolation placeholder `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `html_part` and `body` both call `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` whenever `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, without ensuring `unsubscribe_url` is present in `template_args`. Any existing caller of `build_email`/`MessageBuilder` that sets `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but does not also pass `unsubscribe_url` (for example other mailers not touched by this PR, or future/plugin code) will now raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` instead of rendering the email. This is confirmed by the fact that the existing spec in message_builder_spec.rb had to be updated to add `unsubscribe_url` just to keep passing.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link changed to multiline block scalar without stripping trailing newline
findings.body: `unsubscribe_link` was changed from a single-line scalar to a `|` block scalar, which by default preserves a trailing newline. Since `body` appends this string with `body << "\n"; body << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', ...)`, the resulting plain-text email body will contain extra trailing whitespace/newlines that weren't present before. Using `|-` (strip) would avoid the extra blank line.

findings.title: Misspelled method/translation key name 'stopNotificiationsText'
findings.body: The computed property and its backing translation key use the misspelling 'Notificiations' instead of 'Notifications' (also mirrored in client.en.yml's `stop_notifications` key use and the template). While internally consistent, this typo will persist in the codebase and confuse future maintainers who search for 'notifications'.

findings.title: No controller spec added for the new unsubscribe action
findings.body: The PR adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action with non-trivial branching logic (slug mismatch redirect, notification level toggling, nil TopicUser handling) but no request/controller spec was added to cover it. Only an unrelated small change to message_builder_spec.rb was made. The new behavior (including the non-idempotent toggle noted above) is untested.
